extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists and practitioners interested in public relations, reputation management, and PR ethics
extracted.subtask_description: A case-study style account of one PR firm's practices, controversies and collapse used to assess ethical, legal and professional standards for public relations and reputation management work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with professional conduct codes (PRCA conduct charter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The firm 'had breached four of its conduct charter clauses' of the Public Relations and Communications Association (PRCA) and was expelled from the professional body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the rules and clauses of relevant professional bodies (e.g., PRCA). Breach can lead to disciplinary action including expulsion; reviews by external law firms (Herbert Smith Freehills) may be commissioned and their findings acted upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to general ethical standards of the profession
rubrics_metrics.description: A Herbert Smith Freehills review concluded the firm 'had breached ethical standards' and had 'brought the PR industry into disrepute.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR work must meet broadly accepted ethical norms (truthfulness, respect for rights, avoidance of harm). Firms should have policies and culture promoting ethical decision-making; failure may result in reputational damage, client loss and legal/regulatory consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not incite or exploit racial or ethnic tensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The firm's 'dirty campaign' in South Africa was described as 'playing on racial animosity' and 'inciting racial hatred' to benefit a client, which was a central reason for censure and collapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid strategies that inflame, exploit or manipulate social divisions (race, ethnicity, religion) to achieve client aims; such tactics can produce severe professional sanctions, client exodus and legal/regulatory scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: No creation or dissemination of fake news, fake videos or propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: The company was reported to have created 'fake videos that appeared to be the work of Al-Qaeda' and 'distributed news stories that had the appearance of being produced by Arab media outlets' for the US DoD, and elsewhere was accused of creating fake news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not produce or distribute fabricated news or deceptive media presented as independent journalism. Maintain transparency about sources and origins of content; false or covert propaganda risks legal, contractual and reputational consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use fake online identities / astroturfing
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations included use of a 'network of fake bloggers, commentators and Twitter users' and manipulation of online platforms as part of social media strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating or coordinating inauthentic accounts, sockpuppets or organised astroturf campaigns. Online influence activity should be transparent and comply with platform policies and legal/regulatory norms; discovery of inauthentic behaviour can trigger sanctions and client losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflict-of-interest editing and covert manipulation of public information (Wikipedia, search results)
rubrics_metrics.description: The firm was criticised for 'conflict-of-interest edits' on Wikipedia, removing negative information and replacing it with positive spin, and for using SEO to alter Google results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not covertly edit or manipulate third-party reference resources (Wikipedia etc.) on behalf of clients without disclosure and adherence to the platform's rules. Use ethical SEO and transparency practices; covert manipulation undermines credibility and may breach platform/community rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have appropriate policies for managing controversial accounts and work
rubrics_metrics.description: Herbert Smith Freehills concluded the firm 'lacked appropriate policies for managing controversial accounts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish written policies, escalation paths and oversight for clients and campaigns that could raise ethical, legal or reputational issues. Policies should cover risk assessment, authorisation, monitoring, disclosure and termination of work that conflicts with firm values or law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in lobbying and registration where required
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations of influencing government led to calls for a 'statutory register of lobbyists' and scrutiny over relationships with ministers and officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When engaging in lobbying or political persuasion, follow applicable disclosure, registration and transparency requirements; maintain clear records of contacts and interventions with public officials to avoid legal and reputational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reputation laundering for clients accused of human rights violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The firm faced criticism for 'reputation laundering' for countries accused of human rights violations and for working for clients with abusive records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the ethical implications of representing clients with serious human rights or corruption concerns; implement client-acceptance processes that evaluate reputational and moral risk and consider declining or restricting work that would amount to laundering or whitewashing abuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure to stakeholders about material risks and controversies
rubrics_metrics.description: Shareholders and partners considered legal action alleging failure to disclose 'the scale of the problem in South Africa', affecting transactions and buy-backs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board-level and partner-level disclosure obligations require timely and accurate communication of material controversies and risks. Firms should document issues and inform shareholders/partners as required by law, contracts and governance standards to avoid legal claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance, accountability and prompt remedial action when misconduct occurs
rubrics_metrics.description: Following exposure, the CEO apologised and the firm 'dismissed the lead partner involved [and] suspended another partner and two employees' while commissioning a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear governance structures, internal investigations and remediation procedures. When wrongdoing is alleged, promptly investigate, take proportionate disciplinary action, commission independent reviews, and transparently communicate remedial steps to stakeholders and regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not weaponize media complaint and regulatory mechanisms to silence critics
rubrics_metrics.description: Executives said they used tactics such as making official complaints to the Press Complaints Commission to attack news stories; the PCC ruled there was 'broad public interest' in the Bureau's undercover reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid abusing complaint procedures or press-regulation mechanisms as a PR tactic to intimidate legitimate journalism. Use complaint channels in good faith and rely on factual corrections rather than coercive or strategic complaint-making.
